messages:
melissa: Heads-up — canary deploy (eu-console-v2) showing slowrenders when opening the Metrics pane. Charts stall for ~4-6s, CPU spikes in renderer.
jorge: saw that. reproduces on my EU canary. stack trace looks like a bunch of module parses + large fetch fanout.
priya: any recent routing/quota changes? I remember we tightened prefetch quota last week.
melissa: we changed the prefetch routing priority yesterday to send more traffic to telemetry-proxy for sampled sessions (rollout 30% -> 60%).
jorge: attaching quick grab of network pattern: multiple identical GETs for /widget/chunk-heatmap.* within 10ms
jorge: ```
GET /widget/chunk-heatmap.js 200 120ms
GET /widget/chunk-heatmap.js 200 118ms
GET /kv/cache/prefix?key=heatmap-123 MISS
GET /widget/chunk-legend.js 200 95ms
``` 
sasha: that looks like prefetch TTL is expired + no KV affinity, so each tab open fires cold requests. telemetry-proxy sampling bump -> more sessions hit prefetch path -> surge.
priya: also saw telemetry logs: sampler rate increased from 1/50 -> 1/5 on canary. that multiplies in-browser telem init calls which inlines telemetry client earlier in bootstrap.
dan: so two things combine: higher sample rate + routing priority -> more inlined telemetry code -> bundle parse pressure -> prefetch + kv misses -> stalls.
melissa: agree. my gut: rollout changed routing weight and sampler change cascaded. we should either revert sampler bump or reduce prefetch priority for telemetry-proxied sessions.
jorge: quick experiment: adding a debounce to prefetch kickoff (200ms) prevented the concurrent duplicate chunk GETs locally and cut perceived stall to ~500ms.
melissa: can we patch debounce on canary live quickly? small flag rollout?
infra-bot: deploy 5532109900 to canary started by melissa — status: in_progress
priya: alternative mitigation: set prefetch-quota=low for sessions marked telemetry-proxy in routing policy. that avoids heavy prefetching entirely.
sasha: downside: a few cold users will pay in latency but overall reduces CPU parse storms.
dan: ops question: does KV cache eviction contribute? If prefetch bursts evict useful prefixes, subsequent interactions will miss.
jorge: yes, KV eviction observed — eviction rate higher by 3x in the same window in canary metrics.
melissa: plan:
- emergency: patch debounce and push canary (melissa / infra-bot) ✅
- short term: revert sampler bump on canary (priya)
- medium: add routing flag to opt-out prefetch for telemetry-proxied sessions (sasha + jorge)
- follow-up: telemetry + devex to sync on sampler rollout playbook (dan)
priya: i'll revert sampler on canary in 10m and watch eviction/latency.
jorge: i'll open a tiny PR for debounce + add test for duplicate prefetch suppression.
melissa: thanks all. tagging @sre for visibility.
infra-bot: deploy 5532109900 to canary completed — status: success
dan: post-patch: canary latency drops from 4–6s to ~600–800ms on initial open. eviction rate down ~40%.
melissa: nice. leaving canary up while we implement routing flag. we'll avoid a full rollback unless numbers worsen.
priya: logs show sampler revert lowered telemetry events by ~70% as expected.
melissa: final action items posted to the incident doc, adding a brief note for rollout owners to coordinate sampling + routing changes next time. :memo: :thumbsup:
